note: Re-judged 2026-10-31 by an independent auditor who authored none of e509c7b0a8. RFC 2545 Section 3 re-read. e509c7b0a8 changed only the four ze.conf blocks of test/plugin/rfc2545-joint-subnet.ci: each adds a bgp-level filter { import { final accept; } export { final accept; } } because ff2aac12b0 made an EBGP direction with no policy reject every route (RFC 8212 Section 3), so before it the cases hit their completion deadline with nothing relayed. The diff is additions only: every expect (the 0x20 pair on same-link, the 0x10 global-only field on split-link, entity-off-link and recipient-off-link), every reject of FE800000000000000000000000000009 and of a withdrawal, the TOPOLOGY/WIRE markers and the RFC requirement tags are byte-identical. A final-accept chain names no filter and carries no modifier, and the peers keep next-hop unchanged, so the next-hop field is still decided by the egress link-scope code (linkLocalNextHop), not by policy, and each case still isolates its own subnet condition. The discrimination records on this carrier verify. Verdict unchanged. Earlier judgement, still standing: The partial stands: thirdPartyLinkLocal and linkLocalNextHop are unchanged since the last judgement, so the include case for a third-party global the neighbor table cannot pair still sends the global alone. Re-judged 2026-10-31 by an independent auditor who authored none of 8b062b45a8. RFC 2545 Section 3: "The link-local address shall be included in the Next Hop field if and only if the BGP speaker shares a common subnet with the entity identified by the global IPv6 address carried in the Network Address of Next Hop field and the peer the route is being advertised to." 8b062b45a8 gave linkLocalNextHop a nextHopRouterThirdParty branch that, under the RFC 2545 joint condition only, returns thirdPartyLinkLocal(global): the fe80::/10 entry the neighbor table pairs with the global by device and MAC. New tags TestRFC2545ThirdPartyLinkLocalAnnounce and TestRFC2545ThirdPartyLinkLocalForward assert exact MP_REACH bytes: positive global 2001:db8:1::9 then fe80::9 with length 0x20 (and NotContains the speaker fe80::1 after it), negatives the 16-octet global alone for a peer off the subnet and for a global off the recipient subnet, on the announce, cached and rs rails; checkRFC2545ThirdPartyLinkLocal carries it to interop. Earlier tags unchanged in what they assert (TestRFC2545ForwardPolicyOwnGlobalJointSubnet still pins own global plus configured link-local after policy). The commit removed {partial}, but the include half is not whole: thirdPartyLinkLocal returns the zero address, sending the global alone while the common subnet holds, when the table has no entry, an unresolved one, two candidates, or cannot be read (TestRFC2545ThirdPartyLinkLocalMisses pins exactly that), and refreshPeerLinkScopes states it triggers no re-advertisement, so such a route stays at 16 octets. Annotation restored with that gap. Verdict: partial. Tested: "only if the BGP speaker shares a common subnet with the entity identified by the global IPv6 address carried in the Network Address of Next Hop field and the peer the route is being advertised to." Gap: "The link-local address shall be included in the Next Hop field if". Producer: internal/component/bgp/reactor/link_scope.go::thirdPartyLinkLocal, with linkLocalNextHop.
